audit.whatIsWrong: Every interaction line reduces to "Flawless Duet is her stun setup — dodge it". The two facts that actually decide this lane are absent: Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage only, and Bladesurge both heals her and resets off a Marked target or a kill.
audit.why: Anivia deals magic damage, so Defiant Dance's charge blunts nothing she throws — a charging Irelia is a free Flash Frost target rather than a reason to back off. Flawless Duet is two blades that must converge on you (850 range, 16s at rank 1); off that line there is no stun and no Mark, and without a Mark the 600-range Bladesurge does not refresh. Crystallize is terrain and Bladesurge is a dash, so walling the minion she wants to hop from ends the chain.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, tradeGood, tradeBad, breakdown.trading, breakdown.carry, ahead, enemyWin and the do/don't details now carry the physical-only reduction, the convergence requirement, the 16s and 600 numbers, and the terrain-versus-dash point.

audit.why: Levels 4-5 stay Irelia's — her reset pattern still out-trades Anivia before Glacial Storm lands, which is what both other sources record.
audit.corrected: phases[3].side = Irelia. The other six rows already agree across both layers and the packet.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] is labelled Lvl 3-5 but opens "Irelia hits 3 items into her passive stacks", and whys[5] — the First-item row — describes the 2+ item stage instead.
audit.why: No champion has three items at level 3-5; the real level 3-5 spike is Ionian Fervor stacking attack speed off every spell that connects, into a Bladesurge chain. And the First-item row needs to say what Anivia's first item does, since whys[6] already covers two items.
audit.corrected: spikes[0] rewritten to the passive-stack-into-Bladesurge pattern; whys[5] rewritten to Anivia's first-item spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal appears only in report[8]; no lane advice explains why it matters or when to buy.
audit.why: Bladesurge heals on every hop and refreshes on Marked targets and on kills, so an unanswered Irelia sustains straight through storm chip — missingInteractions flags exactly this.
audit.corrected: breakdown.carry, ahead and dontsFull[0].d now put Grievous Wounds on the clock.

edits.before: - Irelia Flawless Duet (Stun): matchup-defining — Her stun setup — dodge it and the dive falls apart. It governs your forward steps. - W Crystallize spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Flawless Duet is 16s at rank 1 and the blades must converge on you — stand off the line and there is no stun and no Mark for the Bladesurge reset. - Defiant Dance only cuts physical damage; your storm and Frostbite land in full.

edits.after: Irelia wins by converging Flawless Duet on you, Marking you for a free Bladesurge, and healing back through all your chip.

edits.before: Threaten Q until Irelia burns his sidestep tool, land it, then E + auto and walk before the answer — chilled E double-damage is the whole trade.
edits.after: Flash Frost from 1075 while she is charging Defiant Dance — it only blunts physical — then Frostbite the chill and walk before she surges.

edits.after: Poking until your mana is gone with no stun left — that is when she hops the wave and Marks you for the reset.

edits.after: Ahead, cut the resets: storm every wave so she has no minions to hop from, wall her off the catch-up farm, and keep anti-heal on her.

edits.before: Carry by controlling space — storm and wall decide where fights happen, and your stun decides who dies first inside them.
edits.after: Carry by buying Grievous Wounds early — Bladesurge heals on every reset, and without that heal she cannot stand in your storm.

edits.before: Her stun setup — dodge it and the dive falls apart. Bait it, count it, then go.
